MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
GENERAL COMPETITIVE EXAMINATIONS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
SERICULTURE EXTENSION OFFICER UNDER  SERICULTURE DEPARTMENT
SEPTEMBER, 2018
GENERAL ENGLISH PAPER - II
Time Allowed : 2 hours
Full Marks : 100
All questions carry equal mark of 1 each. Attempt all questions.
Directions (Questions 1 - 10): Identify the parts of speech of the underlined words:
1. Let us move on.
(a) Verb
(b) Adjective
(c) Noun
(d) Adverb
2. The play was fantastic.
(a) Adjective
(b) Adverb
(c) Noun
(d) Verb
3. The books are where you left them.
(a) Pronoun
(b) Noun
(c) Adverb
(d) Adjective
4. After lunch let’s go out for a coffee.
(a) Verb
(b) Preposition
(c) Pronoun
(d) Adjective
5. Well, I don’t think I’ll be home before 6.
(a) Interjection
(b) Preposition
(c) Pronoun
(d) Conjunction
6. I will watch while you sleep.
(a) Adjective
(b) Adverb
(c) Conjunction
(d) Preposition
7. That was a difficult question.
(a) Preposition
(b) Adjective
(c) Adverb
(d) Verb
8. Do you like dogs?
(a) Noun
(b) Adjective
(c) Verb
(d) Adverb
9. He worked the sum quickly.
(a) Noun
(b) Pronoun
(c) Verb
(d) Adverb
10. He kept the fast for a week.
(a) Noun
(b) Adjective
(c) Adverb
(d) Preposition

- 2 -
Directions (Questions 11 - 20): Choose the correct relative pronoun:
11. The baby, ____________ nap had been interrupted.
(a) whose
(b) whomever
(c) whom
(d) who
12. This is the place ____________ we met.
(a) when
(b) where
(c) who
(d) that
13. The winners, ____________ known, will receive the prizes.
(a) whoever
(b) who
(c) when
(d) that
14. I saw the shoes ____________ you bought last week.
(a) when
(b) that
(c) who
(d) whom
15. You can choose one person, ____________ you like to share the trip with you.
(a) whomever
(b) that
(c) which
(d) whom
16. The clubhouse, in ____________ the party was held had a large pool
(a) which
(b) where
(c) that
(d) whom
17. I’d like to take you to a café ____________ serves excellent coffee.
(a) what
(b) whatever
(c) which
(d) whichever
18. The police needed details ____________ could help identify the robber.
(a) who
(b) whatever
(c) that
(d) what
19. I am looking for someone ____________ can watch my cat while I am away.
(a) which
(b) who
(c) whom
(d) whoever
20. The festival, ____________ lasted all day, ended with a feast.
(a) that
(b) who
(c) which
(d) what
Directions (Questions 21 - 30): Fill the blanks with proper conjunctions.
21. I was on time, ____________ everyone else was late.
(a) so
(b) but
(c) for
(d) and
22. He is a weak leader, ____________ he has plenty of supporters.
(a) otherwise
(b) moreover
(c) nevertheless
(d) therefore
23. You will be late ____________ you hurry.
(a) unless
(b) when
(c) until
(d) if
24. Give me a drink, ____________ I shall die of thirst.
(a) else
(b) till
(c) if
(d) and

- 3 -
25. Wait ____________ I return.
(a) for
(b) when
(c) before
(d) till
26. My car has a radio____________ music player.
(a) but
(b) or
(c) and
(d) nor
27. I visit the Grand Canyon ____________ I go to Arizona.
(a) once
(b) whenever
(c) wherever
(d) when
28. I could not get a seat ____________ I came early.
(a) if
(b) as
(c) when
(d) though
29. Live well ____________ you may die well.
(a) when
(b) and
(c) that
(d) or
30. He finished first ____________ he began late.
(a) as
(b) though
(c) since
(d) for
Directions (Questions 31 - 35): Choose the correct preposition/ articles to complete the sentences.
31. We should not spend money____________ luxuries.
(a) for
(b) on
(c) with
(d) in
32. They are called ____________ different names.
(a) by
(b) with
(c) for
(d) at
33. ____________ the evening we watched for fireflies.
(a) Under
(b) Between
(c) Throughout
(d) After
34. They will return ____________ Sunset.
(a) after
(b) at
(c) for
(d) before
35. He travelled 70 miles ____________ two hours.
(a) in
(b) for
(c) by
(d) at
Directions (Questions 36 - 40): Fill in the blanks with the correct form of the verb from the given
options:
36. Time and tide ____________ for no man. (wait)
(a) wait
(b) waited
(c) waits
(d) had waited
37. The car crashed when the driver ____________ at full speed. (go)
(a) go
(b) goes
(c) gone
(d) was going

- 4 -
38. David ____________ the gold medal last year. (win)
(a) won
(b) win
(c) wins
(d) winning
39. Yesterday evening I ____________ hard till late because I had a difficult task. (work)
(a) had worked
(b) work
(c) was working
(d) am working.
40. John gave a speech. He ____________ for an hour. (speak)
(a) speak
(b) speaks
(c) had spoken
(d) spoke
Directions (Questions 41 - 51): Transform the following sentences as directed.
41. How gorgeous is the sunset! (Assertive)
(a) How is the sunset so gorgeous?
(b) The sunset is gorgeous, isn’t it?
(c) The sunset is very gorgeous.
(d) How gorgeous the sunset is!
42. No other metal is as expensive as gold. (Superlative)
(a) No other metal except gold is expensive.
(b) Gold is expensive of all the metals.
(c) Isn’t gold the most expensive?
(d) Gold is the most expensive of all the metals.
43. She treated me respectfully. (Adjective)
(a) She treated me with respect.
(b) She respectfully treats me.
(c) She was respectful to me.
(d) She treats me with respect.
44. Human is mortal. (Negative)
(a) Human is immortal.
(b) Human is not immortal.
(c) Not all humans are mortal.
(d) Not all humans are immortal.
45. Stop it. (Interrogative)
(a) Will you stop it?
(b) Please stop it.
(c) Can you stop it?
(d) Please stop.
46. It is too late. We can’t start a new lesson now. (Use infinitive)
(a) It is too late for us to start a new lesson.
(b) It is too late that can’t start a new lesson.
(c) It is getting late to start a new lesson.
(d) We are too late starting a new lesson.
47. Cancer is curable and everybody knows this. (to complex)
(a) Cancer is curable is known to all.
(b) Cancer is curable is a known fact.
(c) Everybody knows that cancer is curable.
(d) Everybody knows that cancer can be cured.
48. Everyone knows that the earth is round. (to compound)
(a) The earth is round and everyone knows it.
(b) Everyone knows the earth is circular.
(c) The earth is round is a well known fact.
(d) The earth is round is known to everyone.
49. Listen and I will tell you all. (to Complex)
(a) If you listen, I will tell you all.
(b) Listen and know all.
(c) Listen carefully to know all.
(d) If you listen to me, I will tell you everything.
50. If you cannot obey me, you have to leave. (to compound)
(a) If you don’t obey me , you will have to leave. (b) Obey or leave.
(c) Either obey me or leave.
(d) Obey me or leave.

- 5 -
Directions (Questions 51 - 55): Identify the following sentences or clauses from the given options.
51. We can wait here until David calls us.
(a) compound
(b) simple
(c) complex
(d) none of these
52. Either the engine starts, or we will remain here all night.
(a) compound
(b) simple
(c) complex
(d) none of these
53. The old car was in a fairly good condition, but the condition of the body was poor.
(a) compound
(b) simple
(c) complex
(d) none of these
54. The small streams that run through the area are loaded with fish.
(a) adverb clause
(b) adjective clause
(c) noun clause
(d) none of these
55. When the leaves begin to fall, we will harvest the last of our crops.
(a) adverb clause
(b) adjective clause
(c) noun clause
(d) none of these
Directions (Questions 56 - 60): Synthesize the sentences as directed in the brackets.
56. He must be asleep. There is no light in his room. (use for)
(a) For there is no light in his room, he must be asleep.
(b) There is no light in his room for he is asleep.
(c) He is asleep for there is no light in his room.
(d) He must be asleep for there is no light in his room.
57. The tortoise is slow. He is sure. (to adversative conjunction)
(a) The tortoise is slow and sure.
(b) The tortoise is slowly sure.
(c) the tortoise is slow yet it is sure.
(d) The tortoise is slow because it is sure.
58. I have some duties. I must perform them. (use infinitive)
(a) I must perform some duties.
(b) I have some duties to perform.
(b) I am performing some duties.
(d) I have performed some duties.
59. He was obstinate. He was punished. (illative conjunction)
(a) He was obstinate therefore he was punished. (b) He was punished for obstinacy.
(c) He was obstinate and punished .
(d) He was punished for being obstinate.
60. He entered the room. He took off his uniform. (use compound conjunction)
(a) He entered the room as he took off his uniform.
(b) He entered the room so he took off his uniform.
(c) He took off his uniform as soon as he entered his room.
(d) He took off his uniform on entering the room.
Directions (Questions 61 - 65): Pick the correct clause in the given sentences:
61. Take a lamp because the night is dark.
(a) adverb clause
(b) noun clause
(c) adjective clause
(d) co-ordinate clause

- 6 -
62. There came a time when he was tired of waiting.
(a) adverb clause
(b) noun clause
(c) adjective clause
(d) co-ordinate clause
63. He gets up early every morning and he goes out to walk.

(b) noun clause
(c) adjective clause

64. He advanced as far as he dared.

(b) noun clause
(c) adjective clause
(d) co-ordinate clause
65. Anyone who comes late will be punished.
(a) adverb clause
(b) noun clause
(c) adjective clause
(d) co-ordinate clause
Directions (Questions 66 - 70): Choose the right collocation:
66. Could you ____________ the oil?

(b) check
(c) test
(d) examine

(b) nuisance

(b) opportunity
(c) offer
(d) occasion

(b) alarm
(c) applause
(d) apology
70. He was involved in a ____________ accident.
(a) ready
(b) widespread
(c) dreadful
(d) risky
